adisesha.description: Adisesha, son of Kadru, is a divine thousand-hooded serpent serving as Vishnu's couch and bearing the earth in some traditions.

aditi.description: Aditi is a mother of the gods and spouse of Kasyapa, described as the mother of Vamana, Vishnu's dwarf avatar.

agastya.description: Agastya is a powerful sage, brother of Vasishtha, who plays a significant role in the Ramayana, guiding Rama and exerting immense influence.

agni.description: Agni, the Fire God, is a divine being and father of Nila, playing a significant role in the Ramayana narrative.

agnivarna.description: Agnivarna, son of Sudarshana, is a character with sons including Shighraga, playing a role in the Ramayana's narrative.

ahalya.description: Ahalya, wife of Gautama, is a pious and chaste woman, mother of Shatananda, known for her patience and devotion, playing a significant role in the Ramayana narrative.

aja.description: Aja, son of Nabhaga, was the father of Dasharatha and a king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, playing a significant role in the lineage of Lord Rama.

akshayakumara.description: Akshayakumara, son of Ravana and Mandodari, is a rakshasa and brother of Indrajit, playing a role in the epic battle.

ambarisha.description: Ambarisha, son of Prashushruva, was a king and father of Nahusha, known for his righteousness and role in the Valmiki Ramayana.

anala.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

anaranya.description: Anaranya, father of Prithu, was a king who played a significant role in the narrative, highlighting his lineage and paternal relationship.

angada.description: Angada, son of Vali and Tara, is a brave vanara and key figure in Rama's army, playing a crucial role in the battle against Ravana.

angirasa.description: Angirasa, one of Brahma's mind-born sages and counted among Prajapatis in several lists.

anjana.description: Anjana is Kesari's wife and Hanuman's mother, a vanara woman with devotion to Lord Shiva, playing a significant role in Hanuman's birth story.

anshuman.description: Anshuman, son of Asamanja, is a king and father of Dilipa, known for his role in the lineage of Raghu dynasty.

anuhlada.description: Anuhlada, son of Hiranyakasipu and brother of Prahlada, a noted Daitya in Puranic genealogies invoked in Ramayana discussions.

arishtanemi.description: Named among lords of Prajapati-style lists in Ramayana-aligned enumerations.

aruna.description: Charioteer of the sun god Surya, son of Vinata, and father of Jatayu and Sampati.

asamanja.description: Asamanja, son of Sagara, abandoned his sons, including Anshuman, in the forest, due to their misbehavior.

ashwapati.description: Ashwapati, king of Kekeya, is Kaikeyi's father, playing a significant role in her marriage to Dasharatha, highlighting his diplomatic relations with Ayodhya.

ashwins.description: Divine twins, sons of Savitri, known for their medical skills and role in Ramayana as helpers of Rama.

asita.description: Asita is the father of Sagara, playing a role in the lineage of Rama's ancestors.

atikaya.description: Atikaya, a powerful rakshasa, is Ravana's son and Indrajit's brother, playing a significant role in the epic battle of the Ramayana.

atri.description: Atri, one of Brahma's mind-born sages and counted among Prajapatis in several lists.

bali.description: Bali, also known as Mahabali, is the Asura king, son of Virochana and grandson of Prahlada.

bana.description: Bana, son of Vikukshi, is a king and father of Anaranya, playing a role in the narrative of the Ramayana.

bhagiratha.description: Bhagiratha, son of Dilipa, is a king who brings Ganga to earth, ancestor of Rama, and father of Kakutstha, playing a pivotal role in the Ikshvaku dynasty.

bharata_1.description: Bharata, son of Dasharatha and Kaikeyi, is Rama's brother and plays a crucial role in the Ramayana, showcasing loyalty and devotion to Rama.

bharata_2.description: Bharata, son of Dhruvasandhi, is a king and ancestor, known for his lineage and fatherhood of Asita, playing a role in the genealogy of Rama's lineage.

bhrigu.description: Bhrigu, the eminent Bhargava rishi, consort of Kavya and progenitor of Shukracharya in Bhargava lineages.

brahma.description: Brahma, the creator, is the father of Marichi and Pulastya, and Kusha is his son. He plays a significant role in the Ramayana narrative.

brihadaratha.description: Brihadaratha, son of Devarata, is a king and father of Mahavira, playing a minor role in the Ramayana narrative.

dadhimukha.description: Dadhimukha, a vanara, is the son of Soma, playing a role in Rama's search for Sita.

daksha.description: Daksha is a Prajapati renowned for his sixty daughters and the yajna later obstructed by Rudra.

danu.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

dasharatha.description: King of Ayodhya, husband of Kausalya, Kaikeyi, and Sumitra, and father of Rama, Bharata, and Lakshmana, known for his righteousness and paternal love.

devamidha.description: Devamidha, son of Kirtiratha, is a minor character and father of Vibudha, mentioned briefly in the genealogy.

devantaka.description: Devantaka, son of Ravana and brother of Indrajit, plays a role in the Valmiki Ramayana as a rakshasa fighting against Rama's army.

devarata.description: Devarata, son of Suketu, is the father of Brihadaratha, a king in the Valmiki Ramayana, playing a minor role in the epic.

dhruvasandhi.description: Dhruvasandhi, father of Bharata's ancestor, was a king and brother of Prasenajit, son of Susandhi, playing a role in the lineage of Rama.

dhumra.description: Dhumra, a bear, is the son of Gadgada, playing a role in the Ramayana as a helper to Rama.

dilipa.description: Dilipa, father of Bhagiratha, was a king and ancestor of Rama, known for his righteousness and role in the Ikshvaku dynasty.

diti.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

drishtaketu.description: Drishtaketu, son of Sudhruti, is a king with sons like Haryasva, playing a role in the Ramayana narrative.

dundhumara.description: Dundhumara, son of Trishanku, is a king and father of Yuvanashva, playing a role in the Ikshvaku dynasty's lineage.

durdhara.description: Durdhara, son of Vasu, is a minor character in the Valmiki Ramayana, with limited narrative role.

dvivida.description: Dvivida, a vanara, is the son of Ashwins and brother of Mainda, known for his strength and role in Rama's army.

gadgada.description: Gadgada is a divine being, father of Jambavan and Dhumra, playing a role in the narrative of the Ramayana.

gadhi.description: Gadhi, father of Vishvamitra, was a king and son of Kushanabha, known for his lineage and role in the narrative of the Valmiki Ramayana.

gaja.description: Gaja, a vanara, is the son of Yama, playing a role in the Ramayana narrative.

gandhamadana.description: Gandhamadana, a vanara, is the son of Yama, playing a role in the Ramayana as a minor character with divine lineage.

garuda.description: The divine eagle, vehicle of Vishnu, son of Vinata; renowned for speed and strength, often depicted carrying Vishnu.

gautama.description: Gautama is a sage, husband of Ahalya, and father of Shatananda, playing a significant role in the Ramayana narrative.

gavaksha.description: Gavaksha, son of Yama, is a vanara who plays a role in the Ramayana, participating in the search for Sita.

gavaya.description: Gavaya, son of Yama, is a vanara who plays a role in the Ramayana, participating in the search for Sita.

guha.description: Guha, a Nishada chief, helps Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita, providing them with food and shelter, showcasing his loyalty and hospitality.

hanuman.description: Hanuman, son of Vayu and Anjana, is a powerful vanara and devotee of Rama, playing a crucial role in the Ramayana as a messenger and warrior.

haryasva.description: Ancestor of Janaka, son of Drishtaketu and father of Maru (Videha).

hemakuta.description: A being mentioned as a son of Varuna in lists.

hiranyakasipu.description: Hiranyakasipu is an Asura king, father of Prahlada and ancestor of Virochana and Bali.

hrasvaroma.description: Hrasvaroma, father of Janaka and Kushadhvaja, and son of Swarnaroma, plays a role in the lineage of Mithila's kings.

ikshvaku.description: Ikshvaku, son of Manu, is a king and ancestor of Rama, known for his righteousness and role in the Ikshvaku dynasty.

indra.description: Indra, king of gods, is Vali's father and a significant figure, often interacting with other divine beings and mortals in the epic.

indrajit.description: Indrajit, son of Ravana and Mandodari, is a powerful rakshasa and skilled warrior, playing a crucial role in the Ramayana war.

jamadagni.description: Jamadagni, a sage, was the husband of Renuka and father of Parashurama, playing a significant role in the narrative.

jambavan.description: Jambavan, a wise bear, helps Rama find Sita, utilizing his strength and knowledge, son of Gadgada.

janaka.description: Janaka, king of Mithila, is Sita and Urmila's father and brother of Kushadhvaja, known for his wisdom and role in Sita's marriage to Rama.

jatayu.description: Jatayu, son of Aruna and brother of Sampati, is a bird who attempts to rescue Sita from Ravana, showcasing his bravery and loyalty.

jaya.description: Daughter of Daksha, noted in lists as mother to a hundred sons collectively called astras and shastras.

jharjha.description: Rakshasa and father of Sundaa, playing a role in the narrative of the Ramayana.

jyothirmukha.description: Jyothirmukha, son of Surya, is a vanara, playing a role in Ramayana.

kadru.description: Kadru is a divine being, wife of Kasyapa and mother of serpents, including Adisesha, playing a role in the narrative of the Valmiki Ramayana.

kaikasi.description: Kaikesi, a rakshasa, was the wife of Vishrava and mother of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, and Shurpanakha, playing a significant role in their lives and the Ramayana narrative.

kaikeyi.description: Queen of Ayodhya, wife of Dasharatha, and mother of Bharata, known for her role in Rama's exile.

kakutstha.description: Kakutstha, father of Raghu, was a king and descendant of Bhagiratha, playing a role in the Ikshvaku dynasty's lineage.

kalika.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

kardama.description: Named among lords of Prajapati-style lists in Ramayana-aligned enumerations.

kasyapa.description: Kasyapa, son of Marichi, is a revered sage and father of Vivasvana, playing a significant role in the Ramayana's cosmogony.

kausalya.description: Kausalya, Dasharatha's chief queen, is Rama's mother, known for her piety and maternal love, playing a significant role in the Ramayana's early narrative.

kavya.description: Kavya, consort of the sage Bhrigu and mother of Shukracharya, beheaded by Vishnu in a dharmic precedent referenced in Ramayana discourse.

kesari.description: Kesari, a vanara, is Anjana's husband also regarded as Hanuman's foster father, playing a significant role in Hanuman's birth story.

kirtirata.description: Kirtirata, son of Mahidhraka, is a minor character and father of Maharoma in the Valmiki Ramayana.

kirtiratha.description: Kirtiratha, son of Pratindhaka, is a king and father of Devamidha, playing a minor role in the Ramayana.

kratu.description: Kratu, one of Brahma's mind-born sages and counted among Prajapatis in several lists.

krodhavasa.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

kubera.description: Kubera, son of Vishrava, is the lord of wealth and king of the Yakshas, playing a significant role in the Ramayana narrative.

kukshi.description: Kukshi, son of Ikshvaku, is a king in the solar dynasty, father of Vikukshi, playing a role in the lineage of Rama.

kumbhakarna.description: Kumbhakarna, brother of Ravana and Vibhishana, is a powerful rakshasa, son of Vishrava and Kaikesi, known for his immense strength and role in the epic battle of Lanka.

kusa.description: Kusa, brother of Lava, both the brothers narrated and recited the Ramayana in the courts of Rama.

kusha.description: Kusha, son of Brahma, is a divine being and father of Kushanabha, playing a role in the Ramayana's cosmogony.

kushadhvaja.description: Kushadhvaja, father of Mandavi and Srutakirti, is Janaka's brother and a king, known for his noble character and familial bonds.

kushanabha.description: Kushanabha, son of Kusha, is a king and father of Gadhi, playing a role in the lineage of Vishvamitra.

lakshmana.description: Lakshmana, son of Dasharatha and Sumitra, is Rama's loyal brother and companion, married to Urmila, playing a crucial role in the Ramayana.

lava.description: Lava, brother of Kusa, both the brothers narrated and recited the Ramayana in the courts of Rama.

maharoma.description: Maharoma, son of Kirtirata, is a sage and father of Swarnaroma, known for his wisdom and role in the narrative.

mahavira.description: Mahavira, father of Sudhruti, was a king and a just ruler, known for his wisdom and role in the narrative of the Ramayana.

mahidhraka.description: Mahidhraka, son of Vibudha, is a minor character and father of Kirtirata, mentioned briefly in the Ramayana.

mainda.description: Mainda, son of Ashwins, brother of Dvivida, is a vanara who helps Rama.

malyavan.description: Malyavan, a rakshasa, is Sumali's brother, playing a significant role in the narrative as a powerful figure in Lanka's demonic forces.

mandavi.description: Mandavi, daughter of Kushadhvaja, married Bharata and played a supportive role in the Ramayana narrative.

mandhata.description: Mandhata, son of Yuvanashva, was a king and father of Susandhi, known for his role in the Ikshvaku dynasty.

mandodari.description: Mandodari, Ravana's wife and Indrajit's mother, plays a pivotal role in the Ramayana, showcasing wisdom and loyalty amidst turmoil.

manthara_1.description: Manthara is a hunchbacked maid of Queen Kaikeyi, fueling her jealousy and manipulating her to demand Bharata's coronation, playing a pivotal role in Rama's exile.

manthara_2.description: Daitya princess, daughter of Virochana, slain by Indra for attempting to destroy the earth; distinct from Kaikeyi's maid Manthara.

manu_1.description: Manu, son of Vivasvana, is the father of Ikshvaku, initiating the solar dynasty in the Valmiki Ramayana.

manu_2.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

maricha.description: A rakshasa who, as a golden deer at Ravana's behest, lured Rama away and was slain by him.

marichi.description: Marichi is a sage and son of Brahma, father of Kasyapa, playing a significant role in the Ramayana's cosmogony.

maru_1.description: Maru, son of Shighraga, father of Prashushruva, in the Ikshvaku lineage.

maru_2.description: Maru, son of Haryasva, is a king of the Videha kingdom, known for his lineage and fatherhood of Pratindhaka, playing a minor role in the Ramayana narrative.

matanga.description: Matanga is a sage who appears in the Valmiki Ramayana, known for his wisdom and role in the narrative, particularly in relation to Shabari.

mayavi.description: Mayavi, a rakshasa, played a role in the Valmiki Ramayana, known for his magical powers and encounters with the main characters.

mithi.description: Early king of Videha, son of Nimi and father of Udavasu in genealogies.

nabhaga.description: Nabhaga, son of Yayati, is a king and father of Aja, playing a role in the lineage of Raghu dynasty.

nahusha.description: Nahusha, son of Ambarisha, was a king and father of Yayati, playing a significant role in the lineage of lunar dynasty.

nala.description: Nala, son of Vishwakarma, is a skilled vanara and architect, contributing to the bridge construction to Lanka.

nandivardhana.description: Nandivardhana, son of Udavasu, is a minor character and father of Suketu, mentioned in the Valmiki Ramayana.

naranthaka.description: Naranthaka, son of Ravana and brother of Indrajit, plays a role in the epic battle of the Ramayana, showcasing his rakshasa prowess.

nila.description: Nila, son of Agni, is a skilled vanara and architect who helps build the bridge to Lanka, showcasing his engineering prowess and loyalty to Rama.

nimi.description: Nimi, a king of Mithila, is the father of Mithi and an ancestor of Sita, playing a role in the lineage of Rama's wife.

parashurama.description: Parashurama, son of Jamadagni and Renuka, is a powerful sage and warrior, known for his bravery and adherence to dharma.

pracheta.description: Named among lords of Prajapati-style lists in Ramayana-aligned enumerations.

prahasta.description: Prahasta, a powerful rakshasa, serves as Ravana's commander, playing a key role in the Lanka army during the Ramayana war.

prahlada.description: Prahlada is a renowned devotee born in the Daitya line, son of Hiranyakasipu, father of Virochana, and grandfather of Bali.

prasenajit.description: Prasenajit, son of Susandhi, brother of Dhruvasandhi, plays a role in the Ramayana as a king.

prashushruva.description: Prashushruva, son of Maru Ikshvaku, is a king and father of Ambarisha, playing a role in the Ikshvaku dynasty's lineage.

pratindhaka.description: Pratindhaka, son of Maru Videha, is the father of Kirtiratha, playing a role in the genealogy of the solar dynasty.

pravriddha.description: Pravriddha, son of Raghu, father of Shankhana, plays a role in the lineage of Raghu's dynasty.

prithu.description: Prithu, son of Anaranya, was a king and father of Trishanku, known for his role in the Valmiki Ramayana.

pulaha.description: Pulaha, one of Brahma's mind-born sages and counted among Prajapatis in several lists.

pulastya.description: Pulastya, a sage and son of Brahma, is the father of Vishrava, highlighting his pivotal role in the lineage of notable figures in the Ramayana.

puloma.description: Puloma is an Asura noted as the father of Sachi, queen of the devas.

raghu.description: King Raghu, is an ancestor of Rama, known for his valor and righteousness in the Ikshvaku dynasty.

rama.description: Rama, son of Dasharatha and Kausalya, is the king of Ayodhya, husband of Sita, and brother of Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, known for his righteousness and bravery.

ravana.description: Ravana, son of Vishrava and Kaikesi, is a powerful rakshasa king, brother of Kumbhakarna and Vibhishana, and husband of Mandodari, playing a central role in the Ramayana as the primary antagonist.

renuka.description: Renuka, wife of Jamadagni and mother of Parashurama, plays a significant role in the narrative, highlighting her familial bonds and tragic fate.

rishyasringa.description: A sage who performed the putrakameshti yagna for Dasharatha, leading to the birth of Rama and his brothers.

ruma.description: Ruma is Sugriva's wife, a vanara, playing a minor role in the narrative, mainly mentioned in relation to her husband.

sabari.description: Sabari, a devoted ascetic, waited for Rama, recognizing him and serving with devotion, showcasing her unwavering dedication and faith.

sachi.description: Sachi, also called Poulomi, is the queen of the devas and consort of Indra, described as the daughter of the asura Puloma.

sagara.description: Sagara, son of Asita, was a king and father of Asamanja, known for his role in the horse sacrifice and the discovery of the Ganga river.

sampati.description: Sampati, son of Aruna and brother of Jatayu, is a bird who helps Rama by providing information about Sita's location in Lanka.

sarabha.description: Sarabha, son of Yama, is a vanara who plays a role in the Ramayana, reflecting his father's legacy.

sarama.description: A rakshasi in Lanka who was kind to Sita during her captivity and offered solace in Ashoka Vatika.

shankhana.description: Shankhana, son of Pravriddha, is the father of Sudarshana, playing a minor role in the Ramayana narrative.

shatananda.description: Shatananda, son of Gautama and Ahalya, is a sage who plays a significant role in the Ramayana, particularly in the Baala Kanda.

shatrughna.description: Youngest son of Dasharatha and Sumitra, brother of Rama, Bharata, and Lakshmana, husband of Srutakirti, known for his loyalty and valor.

shighraga.description: Ancestor of Rama, son of Agnivarna and father of Maru (Ikshvaku).

shiva.description: Shiva, invoked in accounts of obstructing Daksha's yajna and associated with the Pinaka bow.

shukracharya.description: Shukracharya, Brahmin preceptor of the Asuras, famed for counsel and austerities; son of Bhrigu and Kavya.

shurpanakha.description: Shurpanakha, sister of Ravana, is a rakshasa who attempts to seduce Rama and later mutilated by Lakshmana, leading to Ravana's revenge against Rama.

sita.description: Sita, daughter of Janaka, is Rama's wife, known for her devotion and virtue, playing a central role in the Ramayana.

soma.description: Soma, the divine moon god, is the father of Dadhimukha, playing a role in the Ramayana's cosmological context.

srutakirti.description: Srutakirti, daughter of Kushadhvaja, married Shatrughna, highlighting her role in the Ramayana's familial narrative.

subahu.description: Subahu, son of Tataka and brother of Maricha, is a rakshasa who harasses sage Vishvamitra and is killed by Rama and Lakshmana.

sudarshana.description: Sudarshana, son of Shankhana, is a minor character with sons like Agnivarna, playing a small role in the Ramayana.

sudhruti.description: Sudhruti, son of Mahavira, is the father of Drishtaketu, playing a role in the genealogy of the kings.

sugriva.description: Sugriva, son of Surya, is a vanara king and Rama's ally, helping him find Sita, with wife Ruma, and a complex relationship with brother Vali.

suketu_1.description: Suketu, son of Nandivardhana, is a king and father of Devarata, playing a minor role in the Ramayana narrative.

suketu_2.description: Suketu, a Yaksha, is Tataka's father, playing a role in the narrative of the Ramayana, particularly in the encounters of Rama and his brother Lakshmana.

sumali.description: Sumali, a rakshasa, is Kaikesi's father and Malyavan's brother, playing a role in Ravana's lineage.

sumantra.description: Sumantra is King Dasaratha's minister and chariot driver, playing a key role in the narrative, especially during Rama's exile.

sumitra.description: Sumitra is Dasharatha's third wife, mother of Lakshmana and Shatrughna, playing a supportive role in the Ramayana.

sunda.description: Sunda, a rakshasa, is the son of Jharjha, husband of Tataka, and father of Maricha and Subahu, playing a role in the narrative of the Ramayana.

suprabha.description: Daughter of Daksha, noted in lists as mother to a hundred sons collectively called astras and shastras.

surasa.description: Surasa, a divine Naga, is the mother of snakes, playing a role in Rama's journey, testing his courage and resolve.

surya.description: Surya, the sun god, is the father of Sugriva and other sons, playing a significant role in the Ramayana narrative, especially in the context of his sons' interactions with Rama.

susandhi.description: Susandhi, son of Mandhata, is a king and father of Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit, playing a role in the lineage of ancient Indian kings.

susena.description: Susena, a vanara, is the father of Tara and son of Yama, playing a role in the Ramayana narrative.

suteekshna.description: Suteekshna, a sage, plays a role in the Valmiki Ramayana, particularly in the context of Rama's story, highlighting his spiritual and narrative significance.

swarnaroma.description: Swarnaroma, son of Maharoma, is a sage and father of Hrasvaroma, known for his wisdom and role in the Ramayana narrative.

sweta.description: Sweta, son of Surya, is a vanara, playing a role in Ramayana as a minor character with divine lineage.

syeni.description: Syeni is the wife of Aruna and mother of the bird brothers Jatayu and Sampati.

tamra.description: Daughter of Daksha, counted among Kasyapa's eight wives in Ramayana enumerations.

tara.description: Tara, wife of Vali, plays a crucial role in the Ramayana, advising Vali and showcasing her intelligence and loyalty as a vanara and mother of Angada.

tataka.description: Tataka, a rakshasa, was Suketu Yaksha's daughter and Sunda's wife, mother of Maricha and Subahu, playing a significant role in the Ramayana as a fierce adversary.

trijata.description: Trijata, a rakshasa, is Sarduli's daughter and a guardian of Sita in Ravana's ashoka grove, playing a significant role in the narrative.

trishanku.description: Trishanku, son of Prithu, was a king who sought to ascend to heaven with his physical body, highlighting his determination and spiritual ambition.

trishira.description: Trishira, son of Ravana and brother of Indrajit, was a powerful rakshasa who played a role in the Ramayana.

udavasu.description: Udavasu, son of Mithi, is the father of Nandivardhana, playing a minor role in the Ramayana narrative.

urmila.description: Urmila is Janaka's daughter, Sita's sister, and Lakshmana's wife, known for her patience and devotion during her husband's exile.

vali.description: Vali, son of Indra, was a powerful vanara king, husband of Tara, and father of Angada, playing a significant role in the Ramayana before his conflict with brother Sugriva.

vamana.description: Vamana is the dwarf avatar of Vishnu who, as the son of Kasyapa and Aditi, secured the three worlds by taking three cosmic steps against King Bali.

varuna.description: Varuna is the divine lord of the ocean and father of Hemakuta, playing a role in the cosmic order.

varuni.description: Varuni is the goddess of wine, commonly described as the daughter of Varuna and associated with the churning of the ocean.

vashistha.description: Vashistha is a revered sage, advisor to King Dasharatha, and a key figure in Rama's life, known for his wisdom and role in the royal court.

vasu.description: Vasu, a divine being, is the father of Durdhara, playing a minor role in the epic.

vayu.description: Vayu, the wind god, is Hanuman's father, playing a significant role in the Ramayana as a divine being and a supporter of Rama's quest.

vibhandaka.description: Vibhandaka is a sage and father of Rishyasringa, known for his ascetic life and role in the Ramayana narrative.

vibhishana.description: Vibhishana, brother of Ravana, defected to Rama's side, aiding in the battle against his brother, showcasing his virtuous character amidst familial conflict.

vibudha.description: Vibudha, son of Devarmidha, is a minor character and father of Mahidhraka, known for his familial connections in the Ramayana.

vikukshi.description: Vikukshi, son of Kukshi, is a king and father of Bana, playing a role in the Ikshvaku dynasty's lineage.

vinata.description: Vinata is Garuda and Aruna's mother, a divine being, playing a significant role in the narrative as the mother of the bird-like creatures.

virochana.description: Virochana is an Asura, son of Prahlada, and father of Bali.

vishnu.description: Vishnu, the supreme deity, is Rama's avatar on a mission to vanquish evil, upholding dharma.

vishrava.description: Vishrava, a sage and son of Pulastya, is the father of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, and Kubera, and husband Kaikesi, playing a significant role in the Ramayana's narrative.

vishvamitra.description: Vishvamitra, son of Gadhi, is a powerful sage who plays a significant role in Ramayana, testing Rama's abilities and providing him with divine weapons.

vishwakarma.description: Vishwakarma, the divine architect, is Nala's father, skilled in craftsmanship, and plays a significant role in the narrative.

vivasvana.description: Vivasvana, father of Manu and son of Kasyapa, is the sun god, illuminating the world with his radiance, playing a pivotal role in the cosmos and lineage.

yama.description: Yama, the divine god of death, is Dharmaraja, upholding righteousness, playing a narrative role in cosmic order.

yayati.description: Yayati, son of Nahusha, is a king and ancestor of the Puru dynasty, father of Nabhaga and other sons, known for his story in the Mahabharata but mentioned in the Valmiki Ramayana as an ancestor.

yudhajit.description: Yudhajit is Kaikeyi's brother and a skilled warrior, playing a role in the events of the Valmiki Ramayana.

yuvanashva.description: Yuvanashva, son of Dundhumara, is a king and father of Mandhata, known for his role in the Ikshvaku dynasty.
